source_title: SIPs, multibaggers and financial freedom: Lessons from Smart Investor Arena - Business Standard
source_excerpt: From navigating market volatility to building financial freedom and spotting multibaggers, the first day of Business Standard’s Smart Investor Arena at the BFSI Insight Summit 2026 had experts discuss investing and long-term wealth creation. Vikas Satija, managing director (MD) and chief executive officer (CEO) of Shriram Wealth, said systematic investment plan (SIP) inflows supported Indian equities amid foreign investor selling. He stressed long-term asset allocation over fund selection and the continued relevance of relationship managers despite artificial intelligence (AI). Edul Patel, cofounder and CEO of Mudrex, launched a report on tokenisation, exploring its potential to unlock wealth in gold and property, improve ownership verification and ease borrowing costs. Financial educator Neha Nagar said financial freedom meant choice, not just wealth. A ₹3 crore retirement corpus, she suggested, could suffice for many Indians. In a session on multibagger investing, U R Bhat, co-founder and director of Alphaniti Fintech, and independent market analyst Ambareesh Baliga highlighted research, management quality, contrarian thinking and patience. Harsh Roongta, founder and principal officer of Fee-only Investment Advisers, urged beginners to master financial basics. The day ended with financial educator Anant Ladha discussing wealth creation. “The first crore is always earned through active income and skills,” he said.
